name: SRP – E-27 demand price plan (summer)
assumed: Two things, the second a grammar limit. (1) The three demand bands: $11.90/kW for the first 3 kW, $19.97/kW for the next 7 kW and $36.05/kW above 10 kW, per secondary reporting of SRP's 2026 E-27 worksheet; SRP's own price sheet was not read, so the household's bill replaces the figures. The 30-minute demand interval, the 2pm–8pm summer weekday on-peak window and "the highest average kW reading across a fixed 30-minute interval during on-peak hours in the billing month" are SRP's own and are not assumed — and the three-band shape is why this preset is `Tiers` and not `Linear`. (2) The season: this version covers **summer only** (May–October). SRP's winter season has different on-peak hours (05:00–09:00 and 17:00–21:00) and its own lower bands, and `PeakTariff` carries one `eligible` and one `pricing` per version, so both seasons cannot live in one file; a winter month therefore has no capacity component and the site steers on price alone (HLD §3). A seasonal `pricing`/`eligible` in the grammar would remove this note and is D2's call. SRP's temporary $0.0038/kWh reduction on the May–October 2026 cycles is an energy adjustment and is not a demand one, so it is absent here.

versions.assumed: See the file-level note: summer season only, and the bands are secondary.
